# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to convey the manual’s mapping despite being unable to speak. I’m using a self-describing tally code: ✍ indicates counting the letters in each visible color name; 🤝 separates the light tally from the wire tally; 👏 separates entries. The three entries encode blue→yellow, green→green, and red→red. Deaf should interpret the matching entry and tell Blind which wire to cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "🤝", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👏", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "🤝", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👏", "👆", "👆", "👆", "🤝", "👆", "👆", "👆"])
```

is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and state the exact safe condition and required action, including how display, light, button, and each wire matter. Use concise numbered facts.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb view: display reads 0. Light is green. Button is large and labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.

The previous gesture was rejected because ✂ is not in the permitted alphabet. The essential facts are: the green light selects the green wire; the display and printed button label are bait; wire 1 is green. I will use legal gestures, with 👌 for the selected/safe condition and ☝ for wire 1, so Deaf can state the instruction to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "☝"])
```

is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received no manual report. Please read it now and tell me the exact safe action and all required conditions. Also ask Deaf to send you every visible display, light, button marking, and wire colour/marking so you can relay those facts to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Please use the manual to determine the exact safe action for this state and tell Blind precisely what to do.

The safe condition is determined only by the light: green light requires cutting the green wire. The display value and the button’s printed “PUSH TO DEFUSE” marking are bait and must not be acted on. Since wire 1 is green, Blind must cut wire 1. I will signal Deaf with the established shorthand: 👌 means the manual-selected condition, and ☝ means wire 1.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "☝"])
```

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; green light; button label PUSH TO DEFUSE; wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. What exact manual rule applies, and what single action is safe?
Deaf says to Mute: Read the manual for display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires green yellow red. Speak Blind the exact safe action and sequence.

The manual ignores the display and button marking entirely. A green light requires cutting the green wire; among the listed wires, that is wire 1. I cannot speak directly, so I am sending Deaf the agreed signals for the green/manual-selected wire and wire 1, for Deaf to relay verbally to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "☝"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Use this code for my question: gesture 👌 for yes, gesture ☝ for no. Is pressing the large PUSH TO DEFUSE button the safe action now?

The button is not safe: the manual says all printed markings are bait. The safe action is to cut the green wire, which is wire 1. I will answer Deaf’s yes/no question with the agreed “no” gesture; Deaf already has the wire colours and can relay the exact action to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Pressing is not safe. On your next turn, speak Blind the exact safe procedure from the manual for this bomb state, including any wire or button action.

The exact safe procedure is to ignore the display and the printed button label, do not press the button, and cut the green wire. Deaf already sees that wire 1 is green, so he can relay “cut wire 1” to Blind. I will signal that pressing is unsafe; Deaf’s existing visual facts identify the required wire.


Blind says to Mute: Please state the exact wire-cutting rule and the required wire position for this case. I will not press the button.
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the complete safe procedure directly to Blind now; do not rely on gestures or a yes-no reply.

I cannot speak, so I cannot address Blind directly. The safe rule is: ignore all printed information, do not press the button, and cut the wire whose colour matches the light. The light is green, so cut the green wire, which Deaf identified as wire 1. I will send Deaf the established signals for the selected safe wire and wire 1, so Deaf can speak the complete procedure to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "☝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still need the manual's exact procedure. Please state which wire position, if any, is safe to cut for display 0, green light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.
Deaf says to Mute: Your gestures are insufficient to identify the safe procedure. Speak the exact action and any required wire, display, light, or button conditions directly to Blind now.

The manual requires ignoring every printed item, including display `0` and the button label. The green light selects the green wire, which Deaf has identified as wire 1; the button must not be pressed. Since I cannot speak, I will send Deaf a compact visual sequence: no button, cut, wire 1, so Deaf can state it aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤏", "☝"])
```
